description: Foundational document establishing HVT project goals, high-level scope (Atlanta/Dallas/Pittsburgh locations), key stakeholders (FAA, Insurers, Investors), and initial success criteria. This authorizes the planning phase and defines the strategic boundaries before detailed operational work begins.
document_template_primary: PMI Project Charter Template / Standard Venture Initiation Document
steps_to_create: Define project vision based on SMART criteria from plan summary
Identify key stakeholders (FAA, Investors, Insurers)
Draft high-level scope and constraints (CAPEX limits, regulatory gates)
Secure initial sign-off from executive sponsor/investors
essential_information: Define the project vision statement aligned with SMART criteria from project-plan.md (commercial entertainment facility, FAA Part 107 compliance, $500k CAPEX per location)
Identify and document all critical stakeholders requiring engagement: FAA Aviation Safety Inspectors, Insurance Underwriters, Investors/Bankers, Local Zoning Authorities, Veterans Groups
Specify the three approved locations with constraints: Atlanta (Peachtree City Industrial Corridor), Dallas-Fort Worth (South Industrial Corridor), Pittsburgh (Allegheny County Technology Park)
Document the selected strategic path from scenarios.md: Pragmatic Foundation (Part 107 licenses, warehouse infrastructure, custom collision sensors, veterans partnerships, corporate packages)
List all regulatory gates and compliance requirements: FAA Part 107 approval timeline (3-6 months), insurance binding quotes deadline ($50k contingency), cybersecurity penetration testing
Define success metrics with measurable thresholds: Year 2 break-even target, 15% monthly customer retention rate before franchising expansion, incident rates below zero
Detail CAPEX constraints and financial boundaries: $500,000 per location for warehouse fit-out and hardware, separate 6-month operating cash reserve requirement
Identify critical risks requiring mitigation: FAA airspace restrictions near DFW International Airport, insurance coverage denial risk, cybersecurity vulnerabilities in telemetry data
risks_of_poor_quality: Unclear regulatory compliance requirements lead to FAA Part 107 application delays of 3-6 months, pushing launch beyond Year 2 and eroding investor confidence
Missing insurance underwriter engagement results in coverage denial or premiums exceeding $45,000/year, dropping net profit margin by 8-12% and potentially collapsing ROI to -100%
Incomplete stakeholder identification causes regulatory violations with fines up to $10,000 per violation during operations near DFW International Airport

Vague success criteria makes it impossible to measure progress against Year 2 break-even target, leading to cash flow deficits beyond 6-month runway and requiring additional funding at unfavorable terms ($150k-$300k overrun)
Undefined scope boundaries enable feature creep in custom collision sensors and AI systems, inflating CAPEX beyond $500k per location without corresponding revenue increases
worst_case_scenario: Project authorization proceeds without proper boundary setting or regulatory requirements documented, resulting in FAA enforcement actions causing operational shutdowns for 2-8 weeks, insurance coverage denial rendering the business model uninsurable, and total capital loss of $1.5M+ across three locations with no path to market validation before funding exhausted.
best_case_scenario: Charter provides clear go/no-go decision framework enabling investors to approve initial funding with confidence, establishes accountability across all regulatory stakeholders (FAA, insurers) before lease signing, creates roadmap for Part 107 approvals and cybersecurity compliance that prevents launch delays beyond projected timeline, and defines measurable success metrics that enable early detection of retention or safety issues requiring intervention.
fallback_alternative_approaches: Utilize the existing project-plan.md as interim authorization document while charter is being drafted, with explicit reference to SMART criteria and risk assessment sections
Develop a simplified minimum viable charter covering only critical decisions (location selection, Part 107 compliance path, insurance requirements) before full stakeholder sign-off
Schedule focused workshop with executive sponsor and investors to define scope boundaries collaboratively within 48 hours if documentation review is delayed
Engage legal counsel specializing in aviation liability to review scope definitions for regulatory gaps before formal approval from board of directors

description: High-level framework for navigating FAA Part 107 licensing, airspace waivers (LAANC), and airworthiness certification requirements. Defines the compliance pathway to ensure legal flight envelopes without operational shutdowns.
steps_to_create: Map current FAA regulations against proposed drone operations (Part 107 Subpart E)
Define waiver application strategy for each location (Atlanta vs DFW vs Pittsburgh)
Establish compliance reporting and audit protocols
Align with insurance requirements for liability coverage
essential_information: Map current FAA Part 107 regulations against proposed drone operations, specifically Subpart E requirements
Define distinct waiver application strategies for each location (Atlanta vs DFW vs Pittsburgh) considering airport proximity risks
Establish compliance reporting and audit protocols to maintain valid commercial airworthiness certifications
Align regulatory submission timeline with insurance requirements to secure binding quotes before lease signing
Identify specific airspace restrictions and no-fly zones near DFW International Airport requiring mitigation plans
Detail the process for handling sudden national event airspace lockdowns during operations
Quantify potential launch delays (2-4 months) and associated financial burn rates in compliance roadmap
risks_of_poor_quality: Launch delays extending beyond Year 1 due to unanticipated FAA waiver denials or processing bottlenecks
Operational shutdowns resulting in fines exceeding $10,000 per violation from airspace violations
Insurance coverage denial for high-speed combat drone operations due to insufficient compliance documentation
Inability to scale to franchise model because regulatory frameworks cannot be replicated across new regions
Legal liability exposure if flight envelopes exceed certified limits during gameplay sessions
worst_case_scenario: Permanent operational ban or project termination due to inability to secure legal flight envelopes, resulting in total loss of initial $500k CAPEX investment and irrecoverable regulatory trust within the aviation community.
best_case_scenario: Successful FAA Part 107 approval with clear airspace waivers for all locations, enabling on-time launch by April 2027 while securing specialized liability insurance based on verified compliance protocols, establishing a replicable framework for future franchise expansion.
fallback_alternative_approaches: Engage external aviation legal counsel immediately to expedite Part 107 application review and waiver strategy
Prioritize Atlanta location as the primary pilot site due to lower regulatory friction compared to DFW
Utilize pre-approved commercial drone venue templates from industry associations to accelerate framework creation
Develop a 'minimum viable compliance' document focusing only on Part 107 core requirements before expanding to waivers

description: Strategic plan for warehouse acquisition, HVAC safety modifications, and ballistic netting installation. Ensures physical locations meet year-round operational requirements and safety buffer standards.
steps_to_create: Evaluate potential warehouse sites against zoning and airspace constraints
Define HVAC modification requirements for air quality standards
Specify ballistic netting and safety zone specifications
Develop CAPEX budget allocation for physical modifications
essential_information: What specific trade-offs between each decision option must be explicitly quantified (e.g., CAPEX impact of warehouse lease vs modular structures, insurance cost implications of Part 107 licensing)

Which primary decisions (Regulatory Compliance, Venue Infrastructure, Technology Integration) have the highest leverage on project success and require immediate resolution before other levers can be finalized

What explicit connections exist between each strategic decision and how conflicts must be resolved when they arise (e.g., Regulatory Compliance vs Revenue Scalability tension requires documented prioritization)
What specific metrics define success for each of the 8 decisions (incident rates, facility utilization rates, system uptime percentages, brand sentiment scores, franchise adoption rates, etc.)
How does each strategic choice align with or contradict the Pragmatic Foundation scenario path identified in scenarios.md, requiring explicit alignment validation
What assumptions underlie each decision that need validation before final commitment (FAA approval timelines, insurance feasibility, cybersecurity requirements)
What specific risks are associated with each decision option and what mitigation strategies must be documented for high-severity risks
risks_of_poor_quality: Unresolved conflicts between strategic decisions lead to operational paralysis where regulatory compliance blocks technology deployment or venue selection contradicts scalability goals
Incomplete risk assessment causes catastrophic launch delays (6+ months) due to unexpected FAA airspace restrictions near DFW airport or insurance coverage denial for high-speed drone operations
Poorly documented decision trade-offs result in misaligned investments where CAPEX commitments exceed available capital ($500,000 per location constraint)
Lack of clear success metrics prevents performance tracking and early detection of viability issues (customer retention below 15%, incident rates exceeding zero tolerance)
Unaddressed cybersecurity risks for player telemetry systems create data breach exposure with potential $50k+ regulatory fines and 30% booking drop
Strategic misalignment between narrative branding and regulatory compliance triggers community backlash, zoning complaints, or regulatory scrutiny that halts operations
worst_case_scenario: Complete project cancellation due to unresolvable conflicts between strategic decisions, resulting in total capital loss of $1.5M+ (3 locations at $500k each), with no path to FAA Part 107 approval or insurable high-speed drone operations
best_case_scenario: Strategic clarity enables coordinated execution across all levers: successful FAA Part 107 licensing within 3-6 months, insurance secured at acceptable rates, warehouse modifications completed on schedule, and clear decision framework supports Year 2 break-even target with documented pathways to franchise expansion
fallback_alternative_approaches: Create a simplified 'minimum viable strategic decisions' document covering only the top 3 critical levers (Regulatory Compliance, Venue Infrastructure, Technology Integration) before expanding to full 8 decision framework
Conduct facilitated stakeholder workshop with FAA consultants, insurance brokers, and venue operators to validate strategic choices against real-world constraints before finalizing decisions

Develop phased decision approach where initial commitments are made for launch phase only (Atlanta/Pittsburgh locations), with franchise expansion decisions deferred until operational data validates scalability assumptions
Engage specialized aviation attorney and drone liability insurance broker immediately to test strategic choices against regulatory feasibility before committing $500k CAPEX per location

description: Framework governing the selection and deployment of drone hardware (sensors, LiDAR), telemetry systems, and data protection protocols. Balances user experience quality with cybersecurity risks and maintenance costs.
document_template_primary: IoT Security Architecture Framework / Hardware Deployment Plan
steps_to_create: Define hardware specifications for collision sensors and tracking telemetry
Establish cybersecurity standards (AES-256 encryption) for data streams
Outline penetration testing requirements prior to launch
Plan for supply chain resilience regarding custom sensor procurement
essential_information: What are the exact technical specifications for custom collision sensors (detection range, latency threshold <10ms, failover mechanisms)?
Which telemetry systems will handle real-time player tracking and what data points must be captured (location coordinates, session duration, interaction logs)?
What encryption standards apply to all telemetry data streams (AES-256 implementation details, key rotation schedule)?
How many penetration testing cycles are required before public launch and which security firms are qualified for drone-specific systems?
What supply chain contingency plans exist if custom sensor procurement exceeds 90-day lead time (backup suppliers, inventory buffer quantities)?
Which hardware components require redundant safety systems (ballistic netting specifications, emergency stop-zone kill-switch distribution per arena)?
What are the maintenance cost projections for custom collision sensors over Years 1-3 and how do they impact net margin targets?
How will AI swarm capabilities scale with additional locations while maintaining cybersecurity standards across all venues?
risks_of_poor_quality: Sensor latency exceeding thresholds causes player disengagement rates above 15%, directly impacting revenue per session
Cybersecurity vulnerabilities in tracking systems expose customer data, triggering regulatory fines $50k+ and reputational damage causing 30% booking drop
Hardware failure without redundant safety protocols leads to injury lawsuits with insurance premiums rising 40-60%
Supply chain disruptions extend hardware procurement beyond 90 days, pushing launch to Q4 and reducing Year 1 revenue by 25%
Inadequate encryption standards violate GDPR-like compliance requirements, creating legal liability and loss of corporate contracts
Maintenance costs eroding margins by 20% year-over-year without proper cost tracking in the framework
worst_case_scenario: Complete operational shutdown due to cybersecurity breach exposing player telemetry data combined with insurance denial for extreme hazard classification, resulting in $150k-$300k investment overrun and business model insolvency within Year 2
best_case_scenario: Successfully validated technology framework enables go/no-go decision on franchise expansion by Year 2, provides clear procurement specifications reducing hardware costs by 15% through supplier negotiations, establishes cybersecurity audit certification that attracts corporate clients willing to pay premium rates for team-building packages with data protection guarantees
fallback_alternative_approaches: Utilize off-the-shelf quadcopters with standard obstacle avoidance as interim solution while custom sensors are being developed
Schedule focused workshop with cybersecurity firm and hardware suppliers in Week 1 to define minimum viable security standards immediately
Develop simplified 'minimum viable document' covering only AES-256 encryption requirements and penetration testing timeline for launch compliance
Engage specialized drone liability insurance broker to validate safety protocols before finalizing hardware procurement specifications

description: Strategic approach to marketing the HVT concept as 'tactical sport' while mitigating community backlash regarding military themes. Includes dual-branding guidelines and partnership frameworks for veterans groups.
steps_to_create: Develop dual-branding messaging (tactical sport vs combat simulation)
Draft community engagement plan including town halls and grievance channels
Define partnership criteria for veterans groups to ensure legitimacy without political risk
Create media relations protocols for public perception management
essential_information: Identify specific messaging thresholds where 'military' terms transition to 'tactical sport' terminology for youth marketing channels.
Define legal boundaries and partnership scope for veterans groups to avoid active conflict endorsement risks while maintaining legitimacy.
Quantify community engagement frequency (e.g., biannual town halls) and grievance resolution SLAs for residents near industrial locations.
List required media relations protocols for managing negative press regarding combat simulation themes or perceived violence.
risks_of_poor_quality: Inaccurate branding leads to 30% youth participation drop due to community perception of excessive violence.
Regulatory scrutiny increases significantly if marketing implies active military conflict endorsement without proper disclaimers.
Community backlash triggers zoning complaints, legal costs exceeding $40k, or insurance premium hikes over 40%.
worst_case_scenario: Operational shutdown and permanent closure due to regulatory fines from aviation authorities and insurability loss stemming from public perception of the venue promoting real-world combat scenarios.
best_case_scenario: Enables successful franchise expansion by establishing brand trust with community leaders, securing premium corporate contracts through legitimate tactical positioning, and maintaining youth participation rates above project targets.
fallback_alternative_approaches: Pivot immediately to 'Sci-Fi Universe' branding to decouple from real-world politics if community sentiment turns negative during initial town halls.
Engage a specialized crisis PR firm for immediate reputation management instead of internal drafting if regulatory scrutiny escalates unexpectedly.
Develop a simplified 'Safety First' marketing campaign focusing purely on sportsmanship and drone technology if military themes prove too controversial.

document_name: Revenue Scalability & Franchise Business Model Framework
description: High-level framework outlining growth pathways beyond ticket sales. Includes corporate team-building package structures and franchise licensing models for regional expansion.
document_template_primary: Business Model Canvas / Revenue Strategy Framework
steps_to_create: Define pricing tiers and corporate package structures
Establish franchise eligibility criteria and IP licensing terms
Project revenue streams for Year 1 vs. Long-term scalability
Identify key performance indicators (KPIs) for retention and expansion
essential_information: What are the specific pricing tiers and revenue structures for corporate team-building packages including premium branding rights?
What capital requirements ($200k-$300k) must be allocated to build franchise support infrastructure before scaling?
What exact franchise eligibility criteria (financial thresholds, operational standards, location requirements) should regional operators meet?
What are the IP licensing terms and legal framework for franchising HVT intellectual property across regions?
What revenue projections distinguish Year 1 per-session income ($50/player cap) versus long-term scalability targets?
Which KPIs track retention rates (target 15% monthly before franchising) and expansion velocity metrics?
How does data monetization strategy integrate into the franchise model for profitability beyond ticket sales?
What legal boundaries prevent active military conflict endorsement while maintaining veterans group partnership legitimacy?
risks_of_poor_quality: Unclear pricing tiers fail to achieve break-even targets, extending financial runway beyond Year 2
Missing franchise eligibility criteria leads to inconsistent brand standards and operational failures across locations
Inadequate IP licensing legal framework creates partnership disputes and blocks regional expansion
Undefined KPIs prevent data-driven scaling decisions, causing premature or failed franchising attempts
Overlooking capital requirements for franchise support infrastructure strains cash reserves during rollout phases
worst_case_scenario: Franchise model collapses due to poor planning, triggering brand dilution, regulatory scrutiny over IP licensing violations, and investor confidence loss that prevents achieving Year 2 break-even target, potentially causing complete business failure with $1.5M-$3M total capital loss across all locations
best_case_scenario: Document enables clear decision on corporate vs. franchise revenue mix, establishes legally sound IP licensing framework, provides financial projections showing path to $10M+ annual revenue through scalable models, and creates data-driven KPIs that support franchising expansion only after 15% monthly retention is validated
fallback_alternative_approaches: Develop simplified MVP focusing on single location's corporate package pricing before full franchise framework development
Engage franchise attorney to review IP licensing terms early rather than attempting complete legal documentation upfront
Use industry benchmarks from similar entertainment venues (laser tag, escape rooms) as initial reference points for financial modeling and expansion planning
Prioritize securing binding insurance quotes and data monetization pilots before finalizing franchise model details

document_name: Initial High-Level Budget & CAPEX Allocation Plan
description: High-level financial framework outlining the $500,000 per location CAPEX requirements. Includes contingency funds for insurance premiums and regulatory delays.
steps_to_create: Estimate costs for warehouse fit-out, HVAC, and netting per location
Allocate budget for hardware acquisition ($50k contingency for insurance premiums)
Define cash flow runway requirements (6-month operating reserve)
Establish financial reporting cadence for investors
essential_information: What specific trade-offs exist between each strategic lever (e.g., Regulatory Compliance vs Operational Flexibility) that must be explicitly documented?
Which of the five core decisions require immediate go/no-go validation before proceeding to execution phase?
What quantitative success metrics are defined for each decision lever (e.g., incident rates, utilization rates, latency thresholds)?
How do the strategic choices in Decision 1-3 directly impact financial viability and launch timeline assumptions from project-plan.md?
Which secondary decisions (Narrative Architecture, Human Capital, Revenue & Pricing) require integration with primary decision outcomes for coherent strategy?
What specific risk mitigation actions are tied to each decision choice that must be executed post-decision?
How does the selected 'Pragmatic Foundation' scenario align with stakeholder analysis requirements from project-plan.md (FAA, Insurance Underwriters, Local Zoning)?
What explicit connections exist between Technology Integration Strategy and Cybersecurity requirements identified in assumptions.md?
risks_of_poor_quality: Unclear decision ownership leads to conflicting execution priorities across regulatory compliance, venue infrastructure, and technology teams causing operational delays
Incomplete trade-off documentation results in unanticipated conflicts between brand positioning and regulatory scrutiny triggering community backlash or fines
Missing integration points between secondary decisions creates operational silos where narrative branding fails to support revenue scalability goals
Inadequate risk linkage per decision leaves critical vulnerabilities (cybersecurity, insurance liability) unaddressed during execution phase
Ambiguous success metrics prevent objective performance tracking leading to continued investment in underperforming strategic choices
worst_case_scenario: Regulatory shutdown and permanent business closure due to misaligned safety compliance decisions combined with cybersecurity breach exposing player telemetry data, resulting in $500k+ per location losses across all three planned locations plus class action litigation exposure exceeding total venture capital
best_case_scenario: Document enables confident executive approval of Pragmatic Foundation scenario with clear accountability for each lever's execution, facilitating Part 107 license application by March deadline, securing binding insurance quotes within budget constraints, and establishing measurable KPIs that validate Year 2 break-even projections before franchise expansion decisions
fallback_alternative_approaches: Convert strategic decision document into a decision matrix format with weighted scoring for each lever to enable comparative analysis during stakeholder review sessions
Create abbreviated executive summary version of this document (1-2 pages) capturing only critical decisions and associated risks for board-level validation before detailed execution planning
Establish weekly decision governance meetings with cross-functional leads to validate assumptions and adjust strategic choices based on emerging regulatory or market intelligence
Engage aviation compliance consultant to validate Regulatory Compliance Strategy decisions against current FAA guidance before finalizing Part 107 applications

description: Initial register of top risks (Regulatory, Safety, Financial) with high-level mitigation strategies. Serves as a living document for risk management during planning.
steps_to_create: List identified risks from SWOT and Expert Review documents
Assign probability and impact scores to each risk
Define mitigation owners for high-priority risks (e.g., Insurance Broker for Liability)
essential_information: Catalog the top 10 critical risks identified in assumptions.md and project-plan.md (e.g., FAA airspace restrictions, Insurance liability feasibility, Cybersecurity vulnerabilities) into a structured register.
Quantify Probability and Impact scores for each risk based on expert review data (e.g., Likelihood: High/Medium/Low; Severity: Financial Loss >$150k, Operational Downtime >2 weeks).
Define specific mitigation actions with assigned role owners (e.g., Insurance Broker for Liability premiums, Legal Counsel for Zoning variances, Cybersecurity Firm for Data protection).
Track status of critical dependencies required for risk closure (FAA Part 107 approval, Binding insurance quotes secured by March 10th, HVAC safety modifications).
Establish a review cadence and trigger points for re-evaluating risks (e.g., Quarterly reviews or upon significant scope changes like franchise expansion).
risks_of_poor_quality: Unidentified insurance gaps lead to policy denial for high-speed combat drone operations, collapsing business viability immediately post-launch.
Regulatory blind spots regarding DFW airport proximity cause FAA fines up to $10,000 per violation and forced operational shutdowns during national events.
Cybersecurity vulnerabilities in player tracking telemetry result in data breaches, triggering regulatory fines >$50k and a 30% drop in customer bookings due to reputational damage.
Failure to assign mitigation owners leads to delayed responses to emerging threats (e.g., supply chain delays for custom sensors extending CAPEX burn rate).
Inaccurate risk quantification misleads investors regarding the $500k CAPEX per location threshold, potentially stalling necessary funding rounds.
worst_case_scenario: Catastrophic safety failure due to unmitigated sensor latency or collision risks results in severe player injury lawsuits, insurance coverage denial for extreme hazard classification, and a permanent regulatory ban on commercial drone operations at the venue, leading to total insolvency and project termination.
best_case_scenario: Proactive risk management identifies all critical dependencies early, securing binding insurance quotes and FAA approval ahead of schedule; this enables April 2027 launch with full investor confidence, minimizing CAPEX overruns and ensuring operational continuity despite minor supply chain delays.
fallback_alternative_approaches: Utilize the 'Key Risks' section from project-plan.md as a Minimum Viable Document (MVD) if a full ISO-aligned register cannot be completed immediately.
Conduct a focused risk workshop with key stakeholders to validate mitigation owners and probability scores before formalizing the document.
Engage external subject matter experts (aviation consultant, cyber security firm) for specific high-severity risks rather than attempting in-house analysis.
